Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Expectation2: Deliver packages on time and to the correct address
Situation2: A package arrives slightly later than expected, but still within the same day
Story: My phone buzzed at 2 a.m., jolting me awake. It was Sam, my closest friend, sobbing on the other end. He could barely get the words out—his dad had just been rushed to the hospital. I sat up, heart pounding, trying to listen, to be the friend he needed. I knew he wanted me to stay on the line, to talk him through the panic and the pain. But as I tried to comfort him, another notification popped up on my work phone: a package had just arrived at the depot, late but still within the day. My boss had made it clear—every delivery had to be on time, no exceptions, or there’d be consequences. I stared at the clock, torn. Sam’s voice trembled, desperate for support, but the package needed to go out now if I wanted to keep my job. My hands shook as I weighed the expectations—be the friend who listens, or the worker who delivers. The pressure built inside me, and I felt completely split in two.
